summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old female was admitted with right ankle pain, erythema, and increased swelling, diagnosed as right lower extremity cellulitis. She had a history of recurrent cellulitis, morbid obesity, and chronic anasarca. IV vancomycin was started, and a PICC line was placed for continued outpatient antibiotic therapy. Ultrasounds ruled out DVT in both the right leg and arm, with the latter showing IV infiltration. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.1, prompting an increase in warfarin and temporary heparin prophylaxis. She was diuresed with IV Lasix, and her oral diuretic regimen was intensified at discharge. She refused rehab and was discharged home with visiting nurse services for IV antibiotics, INR monitoring, and lab follow-up.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
